# Edit ops and problems

## Edit ops (flow_edit)

Ops run in order, all or nothing: when one fails nothing is written and the error names the op. Name nodes by key (`check-ntp`), steps inside a subflow by path (`fix-ntp/push-config`), ports as `node.port`. A node added earlier in the batch can be used by later ops.

### add_node

Add a node. after continues from an output port: a free port is wired to the new node, a wired one gets the node on its wire (so a chain grows: a new flow is start -> done). on_wire does the same for a wired port only, failed_to wires its failed_hosts. The key comes from the title unless given. Use in to add it inside a subflow.

- `type` (end | task | subflow | decision | approval | parallel | join, required): start (one, on the top level; hosts enter), end (hosts leave; outcome success or failed), task, subflow (has an inner level), decision (true/false per host), approval (a person approves), parallel (branches), join (branches meet).
- `title` (string, required): Human name shown on the canvas.
- `key` (string): Key of the new node; default: from the title. Must be new on its level.
- `in` (string): Subflow whose inner level gets the node (default: top).
- `after` (string): Continue from this output port: wired to the new node, or the node goes on its wire when the port is wired already.
- `on_wire` (string): Put the new node on the wire leaving this output port (between both ends).
- `failed_to` (string): Wire the new node's failed_hosts to this node.
- `intent` (string): What the node should do, in a sentence. Skeleton runs print it.
- `ports` (list of in | ok_hosts | failed_hosts | unreachable | unchanged | always | cancelled | timeout | undo | true | false | approved | rejected | join | string): Optional ports enabled beyond the type defaults (e.g. unreachable, timeout, always on a task).
- `purpose` (rollback | notify | retry | exclude): Format 2: what the node is for in failure handling (rollback, notify, retry, exclude); the patterns set it, and a Rollback is found by it.
- `outcome` (success | failed): End nodes: success or failed.
- `condition` (string): Decision nodes: Jinja expression evaluated per host.
- `branches` (integer): Parallel nodes: number of branch ports branch_1..branch_n (default 2)
- `join_mode` (all | any): Join nodes: per host, all = every branch delivered the host (default), any = at least one
- `inputs` (map of object): Values the node needs, usually from: an earlier node or a flow input.
- `outputs` (map of object): Values the node produces for later nodes.
- `settings` (object): How the node runs (play keywords).
- `impl` (object | null): What the node runs: a module, a role or a playbook. Absent: a TODO stub.
- `position` (object): Where the new node goes; leave it out for automatic placement. Where the node goes: {x, y}, or exactly one of below / above / right_of / left_of naming a node of the same level (key, or subflow/step), with an optional gap in pixels (default 56 below/above, 48 beside); a relative place steps aside until it is free. Positions are per level (the top level, or the inside of one subflow): x,y is the top-left corner of the node box in canvas pixels, y grows down; start and end nodes are 136x40, all others 208x76; flows read top-down. A node without a position is placed by the canvas (auto-layout next to its neighbours) until the first move or tidy_up stores it, so positions can be left out. Placing a node on a level that is still auto-laid out also stores where the canvas shows the others, so nothing else moves.

```json
{"op":"add_node","type":"task","title":"Check NTP","on_wire":"precheck.ok_hosts","intent":"Compare the NTP servers with the standard"}
```

### update_node

Change fields of a node; null removes a field. A new key renames the node: from: references follow.

- `node` (string, required): A node by key (check-ntp), or subflow/step for a step inside a subflow (fix-ntp/push-config).
- `title` (string): Human name shown on the canvas.
- `key` (string): Short name, unique on its level: lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Wires and from: references may use it.
- `intent` (string | null): What the node should do, in a sentence. Skeleton runs print it.
- `status` (draft | specified | implemented): Format 2: the status follows the node (inputs or outputs make it specified, a binding implemented); set here only the status the node already has, which clears tested. Format 1: draft, specified or implemented by hand. tested comes from a passing run only.
- `condition` (string | null): Decision nodes: Jinja test without braces, evaluated per host; it reads the node's inputs
- `outcome` (success | failed | null): End nodes
- `purpose` (rollback | notify | retry | exclude | null): Format 2: what the node is for in failure handling (rollback, notify, retry, exclude); the patterns set it, and a Rollback is found by it.
- `join_mode` (all | any | null): Join nodes: per host, all = every branch delivered the host (default), any = at least one
- `branches` (integer | null): Parallel nodes: number of branch ports branch_1..branch_n (default 2)
- `settings` (object): Settings to change; a null value removes that setting.
- `keywords` (object | null): Task keywords of the binding (when, loop, ignore_errors, ...), replacing the ones it has; null removes them. Needs a module or role binding.

```json
{"op":"update_node","node":"check-ntp","intent":"Compare NTP servers with the standard"}
```

### delete

Delete nodes (with their wires, inner steps and positions) and wires (named by the output port they leave).

- `nodes` (list of string): Nodes to delete (with the notes on them).
- `wires` (list of string): Wires to delete, by the output they leave.
- `annotations` (list of string): Notes, sections or text to delete.

```json
{"op":"delete","nodes":["old-check"],"wires":["precheck.failed_hosts"]}
```

### connect

Wire an output port to a node. One wire per output: fan out with a parallel node.

- `from` (string, required): An output port: node.port, e.g. check-ntp.failed_hosts or fix-ntp/push-config.ok_hosts.
- `to` (string, required): The node the wire goes to (its in port), or node.port for another input port.

```json
{"op":"connect","from":"check-ntp.ok_hosts","to":"done"}
```

### disconnect

Remove the wire leaving an output port.

- `from` (string, required): An output port: node.port, e.g. check-ntp.failed_hosts or fix-ntp/push-config.ok_hosts.

```json
{"op":"disconnect","from":"check-ntp.ok_hosts"}
```

### rewire

Point the wire leaving an output port at another node.

- `from` (string, required): An output port: node.port, e.g. check-ntp.failed_hosts or fix-ntp/push-config.ok_hosts.
- `to` (string, required): The node the wire goes to (its in port), or node.port for another input port.

```json
{"op":"rewire","from":"check-ntp.ok_hosts","to":"report"}
```

### enable_port

Enable an optional port of a node (e.g. unreachable, timeout, always on a task) so it can be wired.

- `node` (string, required): A node by key (check-ntp), or subflow/step for a step inside a subflow (fix-ntp/push-config).
- `port` (string, required): The optional port.

```json
{"op":"enable_port","node":"push-config","port":"unreachable"}
```

### disable_port

Disable an optional port; its wire is removed.

- `node` (string, required): A node by key (check-ntp), or subflow/step for a step inside a subflow (fix-ntp/push-config).
- `port` (string, required): The optional port.

```json
{"op":"disable_port","node":"push-config","port":"unreachable"}
```

### accept

Accept something as it is, with a reason recorded in the flow: a fail port left unwired on purpose (at: the port), a warning from the problems (finding: check:<code>[:<subject>], at: the node; needs flow format 2), a drift item (drift:<item>) or a lens finding (lens:<id>).

- `at` (string, required): The fail port (node.port) when accepting a port; else the node.
- `finding` (string): What is accepted: omit (or port:<port>) for a port; check:<code>[:<subject>] for a problem, e.g. check:binding-unknown-var:ntp_servers; drift:<item>; lens:<finding id>.
- `reason` (string, required): Why it stays as it is (shown in reviews).

```json
{"op":"accept","at":"check-ntp","finding":"check:binding-unknown-var:ntp_servers","reason":"Set in group_vars/edge.yml"}
```

### unaccept

Take back an accept (the same at and finding).

- `at` (string, required): The port (node.port), or the node.
- `finding` (string): As given to accept; omit for a port.

```json
{"op":"unaccept","at":"check-ntp.failed_hosts"}
```

### leave_open

Same as accept on a port (kept for one release): leave a fail port unwired on purpose, with a reason; its hosts fail the run and the open-port warning goes away.

- `at` (string, required): The fail port, e.g. check-ntp.failed_hosts.
- `reason` (string, required): Why the port stays open (shown in reviews).

```json
{"op":"leave_open","at":"check-ntp.failed_hosts","reason":"Read-only check; the report lists these hosts"}
```

### reopen

Same as unaccept on a port (kept for one release): remove a leave_open decision.

- `at` (string, required): node.port, e.g. check-ntp.failed_hosts or fix-ntp/push-config.ok_hosts.

```json
{"op":"reopen","at":"check-ntp.failed_hosts"}
```

### apply_pattern

Handle an output with a ready-made pattern: adds the handler node and its wires (see the pattern list).

- `at` (string, required): An output port: node.port, e.g. check-ntp.failed_hosts or fix-ntp/push-config.ok_hosts.
- `pattern` (rollback | notify-stop | exclude | retry | stop | done | escalate | report, required): Which pattern (see the pattern list).
- `end` (string): End node (same level) the hosts go to, instead of the one the pattern picks: it reuses an end keyed stopped/failed (excluded, done), else makes a new one.
- `position` (object): Where the handler node the pattern adds (for a pattern without one, its new end node; a new end goes below the handler) goes; leave it out for automatic placement. Where the node goes: {x, y}, or exactly one of below / above / right_of / left_of naming a node of the same level (key, or subflow/step), with an optional gap in pixels (default 56 below/above, 48 beside); a relative place steps aside until it is free. Positions are per level (the top level, or the inside of one subflow): x,y is the top-left corner of the node box in canvas pixels, y grows down; start and end nodes are 136x40, all others 208x76; flows read top-down. A node without a position is placed by the canvas (auto-layout next to its neighbours) until the first move or tidy_up stores it, so positions can be left out. Placing a node on a level that is still auto-laid out also stores where the canvas shows the others, so nothing else moves.

```json
{"op":"apply_pattern","at":"push-config.failed_hosts","pattern":"rollback"}
```

### set_io

Add, change, rename or remove (field: null) one input or output of a node, or of the flow (node: "flow"). from: may name a step inside another subflow (precheck/normalize-facts.fos_version): each subflow on the way gets an output that lifts it, and the field reads precheck.fos_version.

- `node` (string, required): A node by key (check-ntp), or subflow/step for a step inside a subflow (fix-ntp/push-config). "flow" for the flow inputs.
- `side` (inputs | outputs, required): inputs or outputs.
- `name` (string, required): Field name (snake_case).
- `field` (object | null, required): The field; null removes it.
- `rename` (string): New name for the field.

```json
{"op":"set_io","node":"check-ntp","side":"outputs","name":"ntp_ok","field":{"type":"boolean","from":"impl.register.ok"}}
```

### ask_at_run_time

Let whoever runs the flow set a step's retries, delay or timeout: adds an integer flow input (or reuses one of that name), a node input reading it (from: flow.<name>), and sets the setting to "{{ <name> }}", in one edit. Delay and timeout are whole seconds. Not for an approval, whose timeout AWX needs as a fixed duration.

- `node` (string, required): A node by key (check-ntp), or subflow/step for a step inside a subflow (fix-ntp/push-config).
- `setting` (retries | delay | timeout, required): Which setting.
- `name` (string, required): The input name (snake_case), e.g. drain_tries.
- `description` (string): What the value is for, shown to whoever runs the flow.
- `default` (integer): The flow input's default (retries as a count, delay and timeout in seconds); without one the input is required.

```json
{"op":"ask_at_run_time","node":"wait-drain","setting":"retries","name":"drain_tries","description":"How many more times to check that the pool has drained","default":12}
```

### update_flow

Change the flow header; null removes a field.

- `name` (string): Human name of the flow.
- `key` (string): Key of the flow (names the generated playbook).
- `goal` (string | null): What the flow achieves, in a sentence.
- `owner` (string | null): Team or person responsible.
- `maintenance_window` (string | null): Longest time the flow may take, as a duration: 4h, 2h30m, 45m (not a schedule or a sentence).

```json
{"op":"update_flow","goal":"Every router uses the standard NTP servers"}
```

### set_entry

Set (or clear with null) the inner step that receives the hosts entering a subflow.

- `subflow` (string, required): The subflow node.
- `node` (string | null, required): Key of a step on its inner level.

```json
{"op":"set_entry","subflow":"fix-ntp","node":"push-config"}
```

### add_exit

Let an inner step's output leave the subflow through one of the subflow's ports.

- `from` (string, required): Inner output, e.g. fix-ntp/push-config.ok_hosts.
- `port` (string, required): Port of the subflow node, e.g. ok_hosts.
- `reason` (string): Optional note shown with the exit.

```json
{"op":"add_exit","from":"fix-ntp/push-config.ok_hosts","port":"ok_hosts"}
```

### remove_exit

Remove a subflow exit.

- `from` (string, required): Inner output, e.g. fix-ntp/push-config.ok_hosts.
- `port` (string, required): Port of the subflow node.

```json
{"op":"remove_exit","from":"fix-ntp/push-config.ok_hosts","port":"ok_hosts"}
```

### extract_subflow

Move connected nodes of one level into a new subflow node; wires across the edge become entry and exits.

- `nodes` (list of string, required): Nodes to move.
- `title` (string, required): Human name shown on the canvas.
- `key` (string): Key of the new subflow; default: from the title.
- `position` (object): Where the new subflow node goes; leave it out for automatic placement. Where the node goes: {x, y}, or exactly one of below / above / right_of / left_of naming a node of the same level (key, or subflow/step), with an optional gap in pixels (default 56 below/above, 48 beside); a relative place steps aside until it is free. Positions are per level (the top level, or the inside of one subflow): x,y is the top-left corner of the node box in canvas pixels, y grows down; start and end nodes are 136x40, all others 208x76; flows read top-down. A node without a position is placed by the canvas (auto-layout next to its neighbours) until the first move or tidy_up stores it, so positions can be left out. Placing a node on a level that is still auto-laid out also stores where the canvas shows the others, so nothing else moves.

```json
{"op":"extract_subflow","nodes":["backup","push-config","verify"],"title":"Fix NTP"}
```

### bind

Bind what the node runs (a module, role or playbook), or null for a TODO stub. Prefer modules the catalog knows.

- `node` (string, required): A node by key (check-ntp), or subflow/step for a step inside a subflow (fix-ntp/push-config).
- `impl` (object | null, required): The binding; null removes it.

```json
{"op":"bind","node":"check-ntp","impl":{"kind":"module","ref":"cisco.ios.ios_command","params":{"commands":["show ntp associations"]},"register":"ntp"}}
```

### move

Place or move nodes and annotations (positions only; nothing else changes). Several in one op, in order: a later one may be placed relative to an earlier one. A section carries the nodes and annotations wholly inside it; a note on a node moves with the node. Positions are per level (the top level, or the inside of one subflow): x,y is the top-left corner of the node box in canvas pixels, y grows down; start and end nodes are 136x40, all others 208x76; flows read top-down. A node without a position is placed by the canvas (auto-layout next to its neighbours) until the first move or tidy_up stores it, so positions can be left out. Placing a node on a level that is still auto-laid out also stores where the canvas shows the others, so nothing else moves.

- `nodes` (map of object): Node (key, or subflow/step) -> where it goes.
- `annotations` (map of object): Annotation (key path) -> where it goes.

```json
{"op":"move","nodes":{"check-ntp":{"x":320,"y":140},"fix-ntp":{"right_of":"check-ntp"}}}
```

### unplace

Drop stored positions so the canvas places these nodes automatically again (positions only). Name nodes, or a level: top, all, or a subflow key.

- `nodes` (list of string): Nodes to hand back to auto-placement.
- `level` (string): top, all, or a subflow key: every node there.

```json
{"op":"unplace","level":"top"}
```

### annotate

Add a note, section or text (format 2): words on the canvas that explain the flow and never run, so adding or changing them changes no version. A note on a node (on) moves with the node, is deleted with it, and its text becomes a comment above the node's code. A section is a titled region behind nodes: moving it moves what is inside. Text is words with no background. The text is Markdown: **bold**, *italic*, `code`, - lists, [links](https://...).

- `kind` (note | section | text): note (default): a sticky note; section: a titled region behind nodes, dragged with what is inside it; text: words with no background.
- `text` (string, required): Markdown: **bold**, *italic*, `code`, - bullet lists and [links](https://...). A section's title; the words of a text.
- `on` (string): Notes only: the node this note is about (its level is the note's).
- `in` (string): Subflow whose inner level gets it (default: the top level, or the level of on).
- `position` (object): Where it goes on the canvas: {x, y} (for a note on a node, still canvas pixels: the note keeps that distance to its node), or one of below / above / right_of / left_of naming a node of its level. Default: a note on a node right of it; anything else right of the level.
- `width` (number): Width in pixels. Absent: the kind's default (note 200, section 480, text fits its words).
- `height` (number): Height in pixels. Absent: the kind's default (note 120, section 320, text fits its words).
- `color` (yellow | blue | green | pink | purple | gray): Background of a note, tint of a section, color of text. Absent: yellow (notes), gray (sections, text).
- `size` (s | m | l): Text only: small, medium (default) or large.
- `key` (string): Key of the new annotation; default: note-1, section-1, text-1, ... Must be new on its level.

```json
{"op":"annotate","on":"precheck","text":"Read-only: **safe** to run again. Runbook: https://wiki.example.net/edge"}
```

### update_annotation

Change a note, section or text: its words, color, size, place, or the node a note is on (on: null unties it and it stays where it is shown). Changes no version.

- `annotation` (string, required): An annotation by key path: note-1 on the top level, fix-ntp/note-1 inside subflow fix-ntp (flow_describe lists them).
- `text` (string): Markdown: **bold**, *italic*, `code`, - bullet lists and [links](https://...). A section's title; the words of a text.
- `on` (string | null): The node the note is about (same level); null unties it.
- `position` (object): Where it goes on the canvas: {x, y} (for a note on a node, still canvas pixels: the note keeps that distance to its node), or one of below / above / right_of / left_of naming a node of its level. Default: a note on a node right of it; anything else right of the level.
- `width` (number | null): Width in pixels. Absent: the kind's default (note 200, section 480, text fits its words).
- `height` (number | null): Height in pixels. Absent: the kind's default (note 120, section 320, text fits its words).
- `color` (yellow | blue | green | pink | purple | gray | null): Background of a note, tint of a section, color of text. Absent: yellow (notes), gray (sections, text).
- `size` (s | m | l | null): Text only: small, medium (default) or large.
- `key` (string): Unique among the annotations of its level, e.g. note-1 or section-2; tools name it by this key.

```json
{"op":"update_annotation","annotation":"note-1","color":"green"}
```

### upgrade_format

Move a format 1 flow to the current format (2). Nothing in the design changes; an op that needs format 2 says so. Run it alone, or first in a batch.


```json
{"op":"upgrade_format"}
```

### tidy_up

Lay out a level again with the auto-layout and store every position (positions only). It replaces hand-made positions on that level. Wires then step round the nodes in their way by themselves; read the layout check it reports for what is left (crossings, labels).

- `level` (string): top (default), all, or a subflow key.

```json
{"op":"tidy_up","level":"top"}
```

## Problem codes

| Code | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| schema | The file breaks the flow schema (a field of the wrong type or an unknown field). | Correct the field named in the message; see the format reference. |
| input-default-type | A host_list or list flow input has a string default; the generated code joins it letter by letter. | Write the default as a list: default: [edge] (set_io on flow with field {type: host_list, default: [edge]}). |
| keyword-reserved | A task keyword in impl.keywords that the flow models itself (register, tags, become, timeout, retries, until, notify, block) or that is no task keyword. | Move it where the message says (impl.register, settings, a handler step, a subflow), or remove it. |
| keyword-ignored | Task keywords that cannot apply: on a playbook binding, or vars on a role binding (role variables belong in params). | Remove them, or bind a module or role; move role variables to params. |
| missing-id | Written by hand: a node, wire or the flow has no ID, or a reference names a node by key. | Run Complete IDs (designer banner or quick fix, or flow_complete_ids). Never invent IDs. |
| unknown-key | A reference names a key no node has (or several nodes have). | Use an existing key; inside subflows keys are per level. |
| duplicate-id | Two items share an ID. | Remove the id of the copy and run Complete IDs. |
| duplicate-key | Two nodes on one level share a key. | Rename one (update_node key); from: references follow. |
| edge-missing-node | A wire names a node that does not exist. | Delete the wire or point it at an existing node. |
| edge-cross-level | A wire joins nodes on different levels. | Wires stay on one level; use the subflow entry (set_entry) or an exit (add_exit). |
| edge-bad-port | A wire uses a port the node type does not have. | Use one of the ports of that type (port catalog). |
| edge-direction | A wire starts at an input or ends at an output. | Wires go from an output port to an input port (usually in). |
| edge-port-not-enabled | A wire uses an optional port the node has not enabled. | enable_port for that node and port. |
| port-multiple-edges | An output port has more than one wire. | One wire per output: fan out with a parallel node. |
| port-not-supported | The port is enabled on a node type that does not support it. | disable_port, or change the node type. |
| port-role-unroutable | A role binding gives no signal for this port (e.g. unchanged). | Bind a module instead, or do not use the port. |
| open-fail-port | A fail port (failed_hosts, unreachable, timeout, rejected) is not wired: its hosts fail the run. | Wire it to a handler (apply_pattern), or leave_open with a reason. |
| decision-no-reason | A port is left open on purpose without a reason. | Give a reason (leave_open again with reason). |
| decision-not-fail | Only fail ports can be left open on purpose. | reopen it; wire the port instead. |
| decision-on-connected | A port marked open on purpose is wired. | reopen it (the wire decides). |
| duplicate-decision | The same port has two decisions. | Keep one: reopen, then leave_open once. |
| annotation-target-missing | A note is on a node that is not on its level (or gone), a section or text is on a node, or the file is format 1. | Detach the note (its menu, or remove `on`), or attach it again; for format 1, Upgrade Flow Format. |
| stale-decision | A decision refers to a node, port or item that is gone. | Remove the decision (reopen). |
| layout-orphan | A position for a node that does not exist. | Harmless; tidy_up or a move rewrites positions. |
| status-overclaim | A status claims more than the node has (e.g. implemented without impl). | Lower the status, or add what it needs (contract for specified, impl for implemented). |
| setting-on-flow | Format 2: credential or execution_environment on a node; the AWX template has one set, on the flow. | Set them on the flow (runtime.credentials, runtime.execution_environment), or let Set Up AWX Template ask. |
| keyword-is-setting | Format 2: a task keyword the flow now models as a setting (become_user). | Set it in Execution › Privilege instead; on a subflow it applies to the steps inside. |
| renamed-field | Format 2: a node keeps a format 1 field name (handler, now purpose: it is not an Ansible handler). | Rename the key to purpose, or pick the purpose again in Details › General. |
| status-out-of-step | Format 2: the stored status is not the one the node’s content gives (a hand edit of the file). | Any edit of the node in the designer sets it again; or write the status the message names. |
| tested-without-record | Format 2: a node is tested but has no `tested` record (a run, or a reason). | Mark Tested… with a reason, or run the flow; else set the status it has. |
| import-gone | Re-import from Source found that the task this step was imported from is no longer in the source; the step stays. | Delete the step, or keep it: remove its origin to make it this flow's own. |
| shared-edited | A shared subflow (a copy of another flow's subflow) was changed here, so it no longer matches the version it was copied from; or it sits in a format 1 flow. | Edit the source flow and Update, or Unlink to make the copy this flow's own. |
| shared-source | A shared subflow's source is missing (the file or the subflow key), is not a .flow.yaml inside the workspace folder, or has a newer version than the copy. | Update Shared Subflow for a newer version; fix ref.from or Unlink when the source is gone. |
| rolling-unsupported | A rolling subflow has a step that needs plays of its own (a subflow, approval, parallel, join, playbook binding, inventory_target, or its own serial or max_fail_percentage), or rolling is set on a node that is not a subflow. | Move that step out of the subflow, or remove rolling: without it the steps run play by play. |
| legacy-port | A node has the undo or cancelled port, which were never built: Rollback wires explicit undo steps, and a cancelled job routes no host. | Upgrade Flow Format removes them and their wires (format 2: remove them); apply Rollback for undo steps. |
| timeout-unreadable | settings.timeout is not a duration the generated code can read, so the step runs without a timeout. A template ({{ … }}) is read at run time on a step, but not on an approval, whose AWX template needs a number. | Write it as 30s, 15m or 1h30m (update_node settings.timeout); on a step, a template of whole seconds reading an input works too. |
| timeout-without-setting | The timeout port is enabled but settings.timeout is not set. | Set settings.timeout (update_node settings). |
| inventory-target-ignored | inventory_target is set where it has no effect. | Remove it, or move it to a task or a subflow without inner steps. |
| host-list-input | A node-level host_list input is informational: hosts come from the wire. | Usually nothing; the arriving hosts decide. |
| no-targets | No flow input seeds the hosts entering the start node. | Add a host_list flow input with targets: true (set_io flow). |
| from-unresolved | A from: names nothing this node can read. | Use <node_key>.<output> of a node that runs before, flow.<input>, or inside a subflow <subflow_key>.<input>; give a path (sub/step.output) to set_io to lift a step inside another subflow. |
| register-collision | A from: reads a register (impl.register) that another step also registers, or that a flow input also names: the generated code reads whichever ran last, and a flow input always wins. | Give one of the steps its own register name (Binding › Register result as), or rename the flow input. |
| ref-may-be-undefined | A from: reads an output of a step that does not run before this one on every path, or that hosts reach after failing in it: some hosts arrive without the value. | Read it after the paths join on the producing step, wire the failure path elsewhere, or give the input a default. |
| binding-unknown-var | A binding parameter (assert that included) uses a variable no input provides. | Add the input the message names (set_io) or fix the name. |
| condition-braces | A decision condition has {{ }} or {% %} inside it; it is a bare expression, as a when: is, so every host would hit a condition error. | Write the expression without the braces: x == 1, not {{ x }} == 1. |
| condition-unknown-var | A decision condition or until uses a variable that is not an input (or, for until, the result). | Add the input the message names (set_io) or fix the name. |
| subflow-output-unset | A subflow output names no inner output, and no single inner step has one of that name. | Set its from to <inner_step>.<output> (set_io). |
| input-unfed | A step input has no from and no default, so nothing gives it a value; the generated task reads a host variable of that name, if any. | Set its from to an upstream output or a flow input (set_io), or give it a default; for the result of a step, make it an output there first. |
| setting-unknown-var | settings.retries, delay or timeout is given at run time ({{ … }}) and reads a variable that is not an input of the step. | Add the input the message names (set_io, from: flow.<name>), or use ask_at_run_time, which adds the flow input and the node input. |
| setting-input-type | settings.retries, delay or timeout reads an input of a type that holds no number (boolean, list, dict, host_list), so the task fails when Ansible renders it. | Read an integer input (set_io type integer), or write a number. |
| until-whole-result | settings.until compares the whole registered result with a value (r == "x", "x" in r); the result is a dict, so the test never holds. | Test a field of the result, like <register>.stdout or <register>.rc (update_node settings.until). |
| until-not-module | settings.until on a role or playbook step, where Ansible cannot retry. | Move the polling into a module step, or remove until. |
| approval-split | Approval outcomes go to different places in a way AWX cannot express. | Route rejected and timeout the same way. |
| awx-segments | Approvals inside subflows, or two that can wait at once, cannot become AWX segments. | Keep approvals on the top level, one at a time. |
| runtime-kind | flow.runtime.kind does not fit the flow (e.g. a job for a flow with approvals); in format 2, it is derived and not written. | Use awx_workflow with approvals, awx_job without; in format 2, remove it. |
| rollback-unreachable | A Rollback node cannot be reached by any failed hosts. | Wire a fail port to it, or delete it. |
| boundary-ref | The subflow entry or an exit names something that is not on its inner level. | set_entry / add_exit with an inner node of that subflow. |
| boundary-no-entry | A subflow has inner steps but no entry: hosts cannot get in. | set_entry to its first step. |
| boundary-port-unfed | A subflow port has wires outside but no inner exit feeds it. | add_exit from an inner output to that port. |
| inner-exit-unmapped | A success port of a step inside a subflow is neither wired nor an exit of the subflow: its hosts never reach an outer port. | Wire it to the next inner step, or add_exit from it to a port of the subflow. |
| success-port-unwired | A success port on the top level is not wired: its hosts stop there without reaching an end node. | Wire it to the next step or to an end node (Done). |
| codegen-cycle | Wires form a cycle; flows run top-down. | Remove a wire; retries use apply_pattern retry. |
| codegen-no-input | A node gets no hosts: nothing wires into it. | Wire an output into its in port, or delete it. |
| codegen-no-targets | The generated playbook has no hosts to start with. | Add a host_list flow input with targets: true. |
| codegen-playbook-ports | A playbook binding cannot route this port. | Use ok_hosts/failed_hosts, or bind a role or module. |
| codegen-segments | Approval segments cannot be generated for this flow. | See awx-segments. |
| codegen-target-ports | A node with inventory_target uses a port that cannot be routed for the arriving hosts. | Use ok_hosts, failed_hosts or timeout. |
| binding-not-in-ee | The bound module or role is not in the execution environment. | Pick another, or add its collection to the environment. |
| binding-removed | The bound module was removed. | Bind its replacement. |
| binding-deprecated | The bound module is deprecated. | Bind its replacement. |
| binding-redirect | The bound name redirects to another module. | Use the final name. |
| binding-unknown-param | A parameter the module does not have. | Remove or rename it (module docs in the catalog). |
| binding-missing-param | A required module parameter is missing. | Add it to impl.params. |
| binding-no-check-mode | The module does not support check mode: skeleton runs skip it. | Usually fine; real runs only. |
